Human. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Cro-Magnon, Denisovan, Florensis, Neanderthal.

This root grants the shared Human core trait package and preserves live UUID compatibility for existing feature items.

“Humanity is not special. It’s just stubborn enough to keep moving when reality begs it to stop.”

Adaptive. 1/Soma Break, when you fail a check, you can choose to succeed instead.

Tenacious. While you have 1 Integrity, you reroll the lowest die on one check of your choice each round (declare before rolling).

Lineage Memory. Choose one human lineage (Cro-Magnon, Denisovan, Florensis, Neanderthal). Your lineage grants Tier powers as you level.

Human Lineage. The branch that kept the reach. Small frames, far horizons, the ancestor who learned that an island is just a problem you can outlast.

“The map says ‘stop.’ You keep walking.”

Florensis. You are the diminutive lineage that survived by being the thing the predators didn’t bother to chase.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid.

  • Size. Small or Medium (choose at creation).

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.

  • Little But Persistent. Your speed is not reduced by being Small. You can move through the space of any creature larger than you.

advancement.title: Florensis Tier I
advancement.hint: Gain your Florensis Tier I lineage power (Little But Mighty).

description.value:
“Small is not weak. Small is opportunity.”

Little But Mighty. You may choose to be Small. You don’t suffer penalties for using weapons sized for Medium creatures.

Hide In Plain Sight. If you do not move on your turn, you can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

⚙ ENGINE NOTE — Pace is now ◆ Surge. Movement banks Surge (capped per round); your courier moves are the ◆ Surge menu's courier kit (Courier's Step / Ghoststep / Flank & Strike / No Such Door + your route's kit). Read Pace as Surge wherever it appears below.

"You're already moving. The fight rearranges around it."

The Shadow Courier runs on Surge, like everyone — but yours comes from motion. Move 30+ ft in a turn and you bank +1 Surge (again at 12 squares, max +2/round). A courier in motion has options; a courier standing still is just a target. The old Pace pool folds into this — same fuel, one number.

The Courier (spent via Surge)

  • Courier's Step (1) — +half-speed move (no provoke) and a freed reaction; flow through the fight.
  • Ghoststep (3) — DR equal to Tier till your next turn, and reposition out of danger.
  • Flank & Strike (5) — reposition, then your next Strike reroll the lowest die and +Tier d6.
  • No Such Door (8) — allies within Tier squares each gain a freed reaction and a reroll; open the road for the whole team.

The Package endures as your work — designate it, carry it, deliver it. Delivery banks your Surge to full and still triggers the route's strategic payoff (Intrigue OP, Darkness reduction, the arrival that mattered).

items.name: Last Mile L1: The Weight You Carry

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Nobody stays behind.

Mode: Psychopomp / drift: Sideways.

Your default Package type is a Soul — a specific character, creature, or intangible (a secret, a confession, a deathbed wish, a refugee's name, an unfinished obligation) that cannot reach safety on its own.

While carrying a Soul:

  • Your movement speed is reduced by 1 square, but allies traveling with you gain +1 square of movement speed (the Soul's witness-weight pulls them forward).

  • You reroll the lowest die on Stealth (Intrigue) and Athletics (Violence) checks made specifically to protect or conceal the Soul (not all stealth/athletics — just protective acts).

On delivery: When you successfully deliver a Soul to safety (the GM confirms the destination counts as safety for that Soul), the recipient faction gains +1 Morale OP and Darkness in the recipient's hex is reduced by 1 point.

You may receive a new Soul any time your Package slot is empty.

system.requirements: Route of the Last Mile, Shadow Courier Initiation 1

You cross what isn't supposed to be crossed — and you always come out the other side carrying something.

On gaining Shadow Courier Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Stealth (Intrigue).

  • Skill rank +1 in Tinkering (Intrigue).

  • Intrigue OP cap +2 and Logistics OP cap +2 on the faction your character belongs to.

  • Pace pool comes online (movement-generated). Max = max(2, ceil((Intrigue value + Shadow Courier Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8. Refills on Soma Break and on Package delivery.

  • Package slot comes online — one Package at a time, type set by your chosen Route at L1.

Pace generation. Gain 1 Pace when you move at least 6 squares on your turn. Maximum 1 Pace generated per turn from this feature. Doctrine features may add their own generators.

Baseline Pace spends (free action, 1 Pace each):

  • Move 5 extra feet without spending an action.

  • Reroll a single Stealth (Intrigue), Athletics (Violence), or Tinkering (Intrigue) check — keep the new result.

  • Ignore a single reaction strike against you on this turn.

Liminal Sense. Once per encounter, ignore the first detection-style roll an opponent attempts against you (perception, scrying, Insight to read your intent, etc.). The roll is treated as if it had failed; resources spent on the attempt are not refunded.

items.name: Route of the Last Mile (Bad Eden)

system.source: Bad Eden Originals — Sprint F (2026 rules)

description.value:
"Give it to me. I carry things."

Doctrine: Carry the unbearable thing to where it must go — intimate, burdensome, exact. Who bears the package now?

The Last Mile is the courier as the one who refuses to let it fall. Your Surge spends take the weight off others: shoulder their wounds at your own cost, carry an ally through a place that should have killed them, and deliver the unbearable thing intact.

Route (spent via Surge)

  • Shoulder the Weight (1) — heal an ally Tier d6; you take half as Stress; they bank a reroll.
  • Quiet Voyage (2) — an ally gains DR equal to Tier, and the next hit that would drop them is held at 1.
  • Delivered (5) — restore a fallen or badly-hurt ally to half Integrity and clear a condition.

“If it lives, you are responsible for it.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Empress (Caretaker). You are abundance under pressure: not softness, but stewardship. You keep people, places, and fragile futures alive long enough to matter.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype nurtures resilience, relief, and sustainable flourishing. This Archetype is associated with +1 Economy and +1 Culture in faction calculus in Bad Eden’s faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

attributes (Archetype ASI)

Common patterns include:

  • Merciful Steward: +2 Soul, +1 Presence
  • Keeper of Settlements: +2 Soul, +1 Mind
  • Builder of Futures: +1 Soul, +1 Presence, +1 Body

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Ashbound Survivors.

“You don’t conquer the wasteland. You outlast it.”

Ashbound Survivors know how to live where maps stop pretending. They ration breath, read heat shimmer like scripture, and treat hostile terrain as a negotiation instead of a death sentence.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Lore.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Economy OPs.

Soul - Creative energy. +1 Violence, +1 Soft Power OPs

Creation arrives all at once. Chokmah rewards decisive action, inspired leadership, and bold openers that turn possibility into momentum before anyone else is ready.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Biomancer / Fleshcrafter.

“You don’t survive the world. You rewrite what Athletics means.”

Biomancers do not treat life as sacred. They treat it as modifiable.

Where Alchemists convert matter and Shamans negotiate with ecosystems, Biomancers operate at a more intimate scale: flesh, bone, instinct, and adaptation. To them, evolution is not a process. It is a toolkit.

The Great Work, in their hands, is not about restoring what was lost. It is about building something that can survive what is coming.

How Biomancers pursue the Great Work:

  • By modifying bodies to survive hostile conditions
  • By reducing loss through biological adaptation
  • By converting harm into resilience
  • By treating mutation as both tool and risk

Resonance: Yesod / Life-State — transformation, embodiment, and the unstable boundary between identity and function.

Tell-tales: asymmetry, controlled mutation, eyes that adapt faster than they should.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on Athletics, endurance, or recovery-related OP rolls

Cost Principle: adaptation changes you. Expect mutation, instability, and moments where you are no longer certain what “baseline” meant.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Empress (Caretaker)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Faith and Diplomacy. You learn the Spare the Dying Tier-0 manifestation.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Tier 1 — Ashbound Survivors

You’ve learned the first mercy of dead land: preparation beats optimism.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Lore.
  • Strategic: In Desert, Ash Wastes, and Wasteland hexes, environmental travel penalties are reduced and hazard pressure is easier to withstand.

Tier 1 — Biomancer

“Pain is information.”

You begin learning how to adjust biological response in real time.

Tactical

  • reroll the lowest die on checks against poison, disease, or environmental hazards

Strategic

  • Once per Strategic Turn, reduce one Athletics, hazard, or casualty-related penalty by one step

Cost: minor mutation begins — cosmetic or behavioral shifts may occur.

Reduce one Athletics/hazard/casualty penalty by one step.

Heavy work jacket, reinforced gloves, and a thigh-strap of tool loops. The standard kit for hex-laborers, salvage crews, scrap-line foremen, and anyone whose day involves both sharp edges and difficult conversations with their employer. Not glamorous. Hard to ruin.

Standard Issue. Counts as armor for protection rolls and as gear for any skill check you can talk your way into calling "work."

item.lore:
Compact crossbow built around a salvaged spring-tension mechanism. Slow to reload, near-silent on release. The Courier's preferred long-touch tool when noise is a tax you can't afford to pay.

Standard Issue. Silent. Slow to reload (1 action between shots, GM call). No signature.

item.signature: Sharpened on a thousand other days like this one.
item.lore:
Standard-issue field knife. Single-edge, thumb groove, hard sheath that clips to a belt or boot. The first weapon most Stewards carry and the last one they put down. Honest steel — no signature, no story, just edge.

Standard Issue. Light enough for off-hand work; close enough for the kind of conversation knives are for.
